title: Beyond Single-Turn: A Survey on Multi-Turn Interactions with Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper is a survey of recent research on multi-turn interactions with large language models (LLMs). It addresses the problem that much of the early evaluation and improvement work for LLMs focused on single-turn prompts, while real-world use in domains such as education, healthcare, coding, and customer service requires sustained dialogue across multiple turns. The authors argue that multi-turn interaction introduces additional challenges including context retention, coherence, adaptation to evolving user intent, and robustness to feedback or conflicting follow-up requests.

The paper does not study a single intervention in an empirical education setting. Instead, it organizes the literature into a task-oriented taxonomy, separating multi-turn instruction following from conversational engagement, and further dividing applications into general instruction following, math, coding, roleplay, healthcare, education, and other domains. It reviews evaluation benchmarks, datasets, and improvement strategies such as in-context learning, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, retrieval/memory augmentation, knowledge graphs, and agent-based approaches.

Because the paper is a survey, its contribution is analytical rather than experimental. It synthesizes findings showing that standard single-turn alignment or prompting methods often fail to transfer reliably to multi-turn settings, and that performance varies substantially across turns, tasks, and languages. The authors conclude that multi-turn LLM research still lacks comprehensive benchmarks for long conversations and needs better evaluation of context understanding, reasoning, adaptation, and ethical/safety behavior.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed-style survey synthesis rather than an empirical study, so it does not provide primary causal evidence. It nevertheless systematically reviews benchmark designs, evaluation methods, and reported findings across the multi-turn LLM literature.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has broad conceptual relevance for how AI tutoring and conversational agents are evaluated, but it does not report direct outcome effects on learners or institutions. Its impact is therefore indirect and mainly informational rather than measured intervention impact.

interventions.use_case: Survey of multi-turn large language model interactions in educational and instructional contexts, including teaching-assistant-style dialogue, educational assistance, and math/coding tutoring behaviors across extended conversations.
